messages:
maria: quick follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/credits — clarity please on how bursting and credits interact for apps using streaming tokens? :question:
phil: good call. can you be specific about the flow you're worried about?
devon: +1 — also curious what happens if a request starts fine and mid-stream we hit quota? do we return partial stream or 429 mid-stream?
maria: scenario: product does streaming chat, user sends long prompt, we exhaust dev credits halfway through the response. do we truncate silently or surface error to caller?
sophie: short answer: we try to avoid truncation. policy is to prefer graceful degradation — send a final message chunk indicating partial response and an error code in the trailing metadata.
alex: to expand: for hosted API we attach a final event like `event: error` with details. the SDK surfaces that so clients can show "response incomplete: billing/quota".
phil: operationally: if dev credits are exhausted we fall back to per-request quota (if any) or the rate-limited path. dedicated customers with reserved capacity ignore credits exhaustion since it's contract-based.
devon: ok — what about `Retry-After` semantics? if we return 429 mid-stream, clients need a consistent header. can we standardize?
billing-bot: FYI: current 429 payload for quota reads: `{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 3600,
  "remaining_credits": 0
}`
phil: that's the present format. product request: change `retry_after` to ISO8601 or leave seconds? ops prefers seconds for easier programmatic backoff.
sophie: recommend seconds for SDKs but include an iso timestamp `available_at` for UI display.
maria: another leadership question — can teams convert leftover dev credits into dedicated capacity trial credits? some customers asked at the event.
billing-bot: policy note: credits are scoped to product type. auto-conversion is not automatic today; requires sales approval.
alex: we're exploring a UX flow for self-serve conversion with guardrails (max conversion cap, 30d validity). IA needs to tie into quota system to prevent double-counting.
devon: roadmap ask: can we expose a per-route forecast in the console showing when a quota bucket will be hit given current traffic? would help teams plan pre-purchases.
phil: agree — Redwood Optimize team has a prototype. goal: show projected spend + time-to-exhaust for each credit bucket.
maria: last: rollout behavior — if we do a canary and the canary route hits rate limits, does traffic auto-failover to stable route?
sophie: default is no automatic cross-route failover (to avoid accidental cost/behavior changes). rollout policies can opt-in to fallback to a compatible model variant/route.
alex: note: fallback respects customer routing policy. e.g., you can configure: `fallback: { "type": "compatible_variant", "max_tokens": 256 }`
phil: follow-up action items: 1) docs update about mid-stream quota exhaustion and SDK behavior (owner @sophie). 2) product proposal for self-serve credit conversions (owner @alex). 3) console forecast UX spike (owner @devon).
maria: thanks everyone — can we sync tomorrow 11am PT to review docs draft? :thumbsup:
